evidence_summary: UMI own-brand wah/volume pedal. Effects Database records Richard Soloway's account that UMI started with a fuzz box and wah-wah pedal, while surviving 1969 examples carry CTS pots dated week 18 of 1969. The precise first-sale date remains unresolved.

Gearphoria identifies the UMI Tone Booster as UMI-made and separately notes that alternate brand versions exist but their manufacturer was not identified. This supports UMI manufacture of the UMI-branded state without assigning the alternate brands.
Gearphoria identifies the UMI Treble-Bass Booster & Mute among the pedals made by UMI. No alternate factory is inferred from related booster products.

UMI own-brand fuzz/volume product is directly grouped by Effects Database with Apollo No. 843 and Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander as UMI-made related states. Kimberly v1 and v2 remain separately attributed to LIMMCO and Applied.
Effects Database explicitly identifies Apollo No. 843 as a UMI-related marketed state alongside the UMI Buzz Tone and Conrad Buzz Box. Apollo is therefore not treated as an independent factory.
Effects Database groups Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander with Apollo No. 843 and UMI Buzz Tone as the UMI branch. This is treated as a marketed-label state, not as proof Conrad operated a factory.

Gearphoria states that the UMI Tone Booster also exists under different brand names but that the manufacturer of those alternate versions was not identified. The UMI-branded unit remains UMI-made; alternate labels must not inherit that attribution automatically.

A specialist Japanese dealer documents a UMI Wa Pedal produced in the 1970s and notes a standard wah on/off switch plus volume-pedal function. This establishes a later physical variant but does not by itself establish the complete production span.
